answers.question: Has the Karnataka Platform-Based Gig Workers (Social Security and Welfare) Act 2025 been brought into force with rules, what welfare-fee rates and categories were notified (Feb 2026), and what is the status of the reported 2026 Karnataka High Court challenge?
answers.answer: Yes, the Act is in force and operational. Karnataka Act No. 72 of 2025 received the Governor's assent on 11 Sep 2025, was gazetted on 12 Sep 2025 and is deemed in force from 30 May 2025 (s.1(2), replacing Ordinance 04 of 2025); the Karnataka Platform Based Gig Workers (Social Security and Welfare) Rules, 2025 were notified on 19 Nov 2025 (No. LD 413 LET 2023, Gazette Part IVA No. 739 of 20 Nov 2025) and took effect on publication; the 16-member Welfare Board was constituted by notification on 27 Jan 2026 with a 45-day window for aggregators to register. The welfare-fee order under s.20 was issued on 13 Feb 2026 and set every notified category at 1% of the payout per transaction (the Act allows 1-5%) with per-transaction rupee caps: ride-hailing Rs 0.50 (2W) / Rs 0.75 (3W) / Rs 1.00 (4W); food and grocery delivery Rs 0.50 (2W); logistics Rs 0.50 (2W) / Rs 0.75 (3W) / Rs 1.00 (LCV) / Rs 1.50 (HCV); e-marketplace Rs 0.50 (2W) / Rs 0.75 (3W) / Rs 1.00 (LCV); professional activity providers Rs 1.50 (any vehicle). The fee is charged on the aggregator/platform (workers keep 100% of payouts), is self-declared and remitted within 5 working days of each quarter-end, excludes tips/incentives/referral 'settled payments' (Rule 17), and platforms may self-report payouts quarterly until the PWFVS portal is live (s.21 proviso); no rate has been reported for the Schedule's healthcare, travel-and-hospitality or content-and-media categories, which is an open item. The High Court challenge is real and pending: IAMAI, Eternal (Zomato/Blinkit), Swiggy, Zepto, Urban Company and Valmo Transportation filed WP 19746/2026 in late June 2026 (27-29 Jun) arguing the Act is repugnant to the Code on Social Security 2020 under Article 254, and the Union of India's ASG supported them in court; on 3 Jul 2026 Justice M. Nagaprasanna refused to stay the Act, ordered the petitioners to deposit the April-June quarter's fee with the Court registry by 23 Jul 2026, barred coercive steps against them in the meantime, set objections by 31 Jul and rejoinder by 10 Aug, and listed the matter for 14 Aug 2026. Uber's separate WP 19776/2026 received the same interim protection on 28 Jul 2026 (Justice Suraj Govindaraj), with three weeks to deposit, notice returnable 24 Aug 2026 and tagging with the IAMAI batch. As of the last public reporting on 31 Aug 2026, six platforms had deposited about Rs 4 crore with the Court for the April-June quarter, 15 platforms covering roughly 7 lakh workers had registered with the Board, Yulu paid the Board directly, and Uber, Eternal and Porter had resigned from the Board; no judgment or stay has been reported, and I could not find what happened at the 14 Aug and 24 Aug listings (open item). Practical reading for 29 Sep 2026: the law binds every aggregator and platform in Karnataka now; only the named petitioners have court cover, and even they must put the money down.
answers.decision: Plan as if the Karnataka Act fully applies from pilot day one (13 Oct 2026): register with the Board, upload Saathi data, and budget 1% of Saathi payouts capped at Rs 0.50-1.50 per job (a few thousand rupees a month at pilot scale); do not bank on the High Court striking the Act down.
answers.whoToAsk: Check the current stage of WP 19746/2026 and WP 19776/2026 on the Karnataka High Court case-status portal or via counsel (nothing public after 31 Aug 2026); ask the Karnataka Platform Based Gig Workers Welfare Board (Labour Department, Bengaluru) whether rates have been notified for the Schedule categories absent from the 13 Feb 2026 order.

answers.question: Is a scrap-pickup marketplace or a Saathi job board an 'aggregator' or 'e-marketplace' under the Karnataka Act and under the Social Security Code's Seventh Schedule and the Social Security (Central) Rules 2026, if the kabadiwala pays the Saathi directly rather than the platform? If so, which fee category, who pays, and does the internal dispute committee duty apply?
answers.answer: Almost certainly yes, and the payment route does not take Luma.Green outside either law. Both definitions are payment-agnostic: the Karnataka Act s.2(b) makes an 'aggregator' any 'digital intermediary for a buyer of goods or user of a service to connect with the seller or the service provider' (plus any entity that coordinates with aggregators), and the Code s.2(2) wording is near-identical; a Saathi job board connects kabadiwalas (users of pickup/sorting services) with Saathis (service providers) and the scrap marketplace connects buyers and sellers of goods, so both limbs are met, and Karnataka independently catches Luma.Green as a 'platform' (s.2(g): a service arranged electronically that organises work by individuals at a location for payment using data-driven or automated decisions), with s.1(3)(ii) applying the Act to every platform. Saathis are 'gig workers' (s.2(e)) only if the work is in a Schedule service: pickups fit item 3 'Logistics services' and the marketplace fits item 4 'e-Market place... B2B/B2C'; sorting shifts fit item 5 'Professional activity provider' less cleanly, and Karnataka's Schedule has only eight entries with no residual category (the central Seventh Schedule has nine, including 'any other goods and services provider platform'), although the Rules' Form A quarterly return does carry 'Warehousing' and 'Any other not in the category' rows. Under the 13 Feb 2026 order the Karnataka fee for pickups is 1% of each payout capped at Rs 0.50 per 2W logistics job (Rs 0.75 3W, Rs 1.00 LCV, Rs 1.50 HCV) and Rs 1.50 per professional-services job, e.g. 10 Saathis x 20 pickups x 26 days = 5,200 jobs, about Rs 2,600 a month at most; it is charged on the aggregator/platform (s.20(1)), not on the Saathi and not on the kabadiwala, who is not a digital intermediary, and s.20(5) makes whatever Karnataka collects count toward the central s.114(4) contribution so there is no double payment. The direct-pay wrinkle is real: s.2(f) defines 'payout' as final payments 'made by the aggregator or platform to the gig worker', so on a literal reading a kabadiwala-pays-cash model has no payout and a zero fee base, but s.21 requires 'all payments made to workers generated on platform' to be mapped to PWFVS and s.15 assumes the platform itself pays at least weekly, so the Board is likely to treat the kabadiwala's payment as the payout and the rest of the Act's machinery presupposes it; this is the one point only counsel or the Board can settle. Under the central Code, Luma.Green is an aggregator in Seventh Schedule categories 3 (logistics), 4 (e-marketplace B2B/B2C) and/or 9 (any other), and Saathis are platform workers under s.2(60)-(61); the money obligation (s.114(4): 1-2% of annual turnover, capped at 5% of amounts 'paid or payable by an aggregator' to gig and platform workers, which would be near zero if Luma.Green pays them nothing) is dormant because the s.114(5) commencement date has not been notified as of September 2026, but the registration duties are live under the Social Security (Central) Rules 2026 (G.S.R. 344(E), 8 May 2026): Rule 48(2)(b) gave 45 days (to about 22 Jun 2026) to upload existing workers, Rule 48(2)(c) requires real-time or daily API registration of new workers and exits, Rule 49(5) requires the aggregator to register on the designated portal, and once contributions start Form XX self-assessment is due by 30 June and Form XXI return by 31 October, with 1% per month interest on late payment (Rule 49(2)). The IDRC duty does apply and has no size threshold: s.22(2) and Rule 21 require every registered aggregator or platform to constitute a committee of 1 senior-management chairperson, 2 management members and at least 3 senior gig workers, with at least 2 women; grievances about payouts, deductions or termination must be filed within 7 working days (Rule 11(1)), the committee must issue a written action-taken report within 14 days and a final order within 45 days (s.22(4),(6); Rule 22(2)), and the worker can appeal to the Board's authorised person within 30 days (Rule 11(3)). The app must also carry the grievance-portal link and disclosures in Kannada and English (s.17, s.22(2) proviso, Rule 13), a human point of contact (s.18), 14-day written notice before deactivation (s.14), at-least-weekly pay with deductions explained (s.15), Saathi database updates within 7 days (Rule 8), PWFVS uploads within 7 days of each transaction (Rule 20), the fee within 5 working days of quarter-end (Rule 17) and a Form A return within 30 working days of quarter-end (Rule 29). Penalties are 12% p.a. interest on late fee and fines up to Rs 5,000 for a first contravention and Rs 1 lakh thereafter (s.23), but the larger exposure is Rule 7(7), under which the Board can order an unregistered platform to produce work histories of every gig worker since the Act commenced and to deposit the fee for all of them.
answers.decision: Treat Luma.Green as an 'aggregator' and a 'platform' under both the Karnataka Act and the central Code from 13 Oct 2026 regardless of who pays the Saathi: register with the Karnataka Board under 'Logistics services - 2W' for pickups and 'Professional activity provider' for sorting (record vehicle type per job so the cap is computable), treat the kabadiwala's recorded cash/UPI amount as the payout, self-report quarterly and remit 1% capped per job, constitute a 6-person IDRC (3 senior Saathis, at least 2 women) and put the grievance link plus Kannada/English disclosures in the Saathi app before launch; register on the central designated portal and upload Saathi details, budgeting Rs 0 central contribution until s.114(5) is notified.
answers.whoToAsk: A Bengaluru labour/platform-law counsel for one written opinion on whether a direct-pay job board creates a 'payout' under s.2(f)/s.20 (and whether to route Saathi payments through Luma.Green's ledger or in-app UPI to make the base clean) and whether sorting falls under Schedule item 5; then the Karnataka Platform Based Gig Workers Welfare Board (Labour Department, Bengaluru) to confirm the registration category under Rule 7(2)(h) and the interim self-reporting format.
